bull.b: Arm's licensing-and-royalty business yields extremely high gross margins and minimal manufacturing capital needs, creating durable operating leverage. This model supports strong long-term free cash flow generation and allows investment in R&D and ecosystem expansion without heavy capex burdens.

bull.t: Robust cash generation and low leverage
bull.b: Consistent, sizable free cash flow and very low net leverage provide financial flexibility to fund R&D, ecosystem programs, and the AGI CPU ramp. A strong balance sheet reduces refinancing risk and supports multi-year investments that underpin secular growth in AI and data-center markets.

Rapid adoption in data-center and AI infrastructure—validated by >100% royalty growth and major cloud partners—signals structural TAM expansion. This diversifies revenue away from cyclical end markets and creates sticky, royalty-based streams as server deployments scale over years.

bear.b: Smartphone demand and BOM cost swings remain a persistent headwind for royalty growth because handsets are still a meaningful royalty base. Cyclical softness or higher component costs can depress near- and medium-term royalty volumes and make overall revenue growth more volatile.

bear.t: Supply constraints for AGI CPU ramp
bear.b: Material supply-chain limits (foundry wafers, substrates, test capacity and memory) could cap the pace at which Arm realizes AGI CPU demand. Persistent constraints delay revenue scaling and margin improvement, making multi-year growth dependent on external capacity expansion timelines.

bear.t: Initial AGI CPU margins and elevated OpEx
bear.b: Early-generation AGI CPU silicon will dilute Arm's historically high gross margins and require sustained R&D and platform investment. Elevated OpEx and a multi-year margin improvement path mean near-term operating margins may remain under pressure until volume scale and cost improvements materialize.
